source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-05 (debate 9): Paley-type doubling (Colbourn 2015) of the Paley matrix over GF(121) via CAs:::Double(CAs::paley_mat(121)) (CAs 0.24.4), giving CA(242; 5, 122, 2); then rows deleted one at a time (two random, then the row with the fewest unique 5-way interactions), each step repaired by single-cell flips (programs/rep.c, uniqcount.c); exact check with ca_verify, all 5-sets
construction: Paley-type doubling over GF(121) then one-row-at-a-time deletion and repair
notes: beats the Torres-Jimenez size 241 (k = 115 to 122) by 3 rows; prime-power q = 121 is not in the CAs Paley catalogue; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start

source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-05 (debate 9): our own CA(108; 4, 113, 2) (row elimination, tools/own_arrays/nck.c, of the Paley array for q = 113, after Nayeri, Colbourn and Konjevod 2013) plus one column filled by the ExtendCA greedy rule (Torres-Jimenez and Avila-George, SBSTT), then fixed-temperature simulated annealing (programs/bsa4x.c); exact check with ca_verify, all 4-sets
construction: Paley array after row elimination plus one greedy column then simulated annealing
notes: beats the Torres-Jimenez size 109 at k = 114 by 1 row; SBSTT is credited as a method; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start

source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-05 (debate 9): the Paley matrix of order 89 without its first row, CA(88; 4, 89, 2), plus 4 random rows and one column filled by the ExtendCA greedy rule (Torres-Jimenez and Avila-George, SBSTT), then fixed-temperature simulated annealing (programs/bsa4x.c); exact check with ca_verify, all 4-sets
construction: Paley array plus spare rows and one greedy column then simulated annealing
notes: ties the Torres-Jimenez size 92 at k = 90; SBSTT is credited as a method; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start

source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-05 (debate 9): generalized direct product (tools/own_arrays/prod2.py; Colbourn and Torres-Jimenez 2013, Cor. 4.3) of our own CA(12; 2, 7, 3) (built by caex.c from the Bose OA(9; 2, 4, 3)) and the table's own CA(15; 2, 20, 3) (CA_15_2_20_3_fd13075b), giving CA(25; 2, 140, 3); column extension at fixed N (programs/caex.c after the CA Extender of Torres-Jimenez, Acevedo-Juarez and Avila-George 2021, with the annealing of Avila-George, Torres-Jimenez and Hernandez 2012) to 209 columns; then column large-neighbourhood search (programs/pool.c, kcl.c, lns3.py) to 220 columns; exact check with ca_verify, all column pairs
construction: Generalized direct product of our arrays then column extension then column large-neighbourhood search
notes: beats the Torres-Jimenez size 25 at k = 216 by 4 columns (k = 217 to 220 at 25 rows); the ingredient CA(12; 2, 7, 3) was built here and has the same fingerprint as a Torres-Jimenez array of that size (essentially unique; six independent builds agree), the final array matches none
